title: Download the course package

blocks.what_we_do:
Download and extract the whole source project from its GitHub branch. Then get the matching encrypted data archive through the approved course channel. Follow these actions for the project:

1. Open the GitHub page of the course branch that your instructor gives you. GitHub is a website that stores project files. A branch is one line of versions of a project.
2. Click the green "Code" button. Then click "Download ZIP".
3. Extract the ZIP file into a folder where you can save files, for example in Documents. Use the same method as at step 0.4.
4. Open the extracted folder. You should see the files `config.R` and `GWAS_training_session.Rproj`, and folders such as `R`, `lessons` and `scripts`.

Keep the whole folder together. Do not move single files out of it.

The GitHub Release (the page that will hold the data archive) does not exist yet. The current archive is a local author test. Its checksums are marked as test values in `config.R`.
blocks.why: The source project contains code and text. The encrypted package contains the data. A [checksum](../docs/glossary.md#checksum) is a short code calculated from a file. If the file changes, the code changes. Checksums detect changed or damaged downloads. The password decrypts the archive. A correct password does not replace the checksum check.
blocks.you_need:
The complete project folder, R and the approved archive. Save the archive (`course-data-2026.1.zip`) and its small file `MANIFEST.tsv` together in one folder, for example your Downloads folder. 

Request the password with your university email through the [data access form](https://manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/data-access). This is a placeholder address until the form is published. In class, you can scan the QR code to open the same form. The form sends the password automatically only to addresses ending in `@unipi.it` or `@studenti.unipi.it`. Other users should write to [manuel.gentiluomo@unipi.it](mailto:manuel.gentiluomo@unipi.it). The password changes every academic year. Do not share it. It never appears in the repository or on the site.
blocks.command:
Run the following commands in the RStudio console after you open the project. If you have not opened it yet, do step 0.6 first and then return here. The commands do not run automatically when this notebook is rendered:

```{r s0-5_data, eval=FALSE}
source("R/package_setup.R")
install_course_packages()
source("R/course.R")
# Only after the public release is published: remove the # at the start of the next line.
# download_course_data()
```

The first run of `install_course_packages()` can take several minutes and print many lines. Wait until the `>` prompt returns.

Until the public release exists, use this command. It reads the archive from your computer and makes no network download. Replace the text in quotes with the place where you saved the ZIP file. Write the path with forward slashes (/), also on Windows:

```{r s0-5_local, eval=FALSE}
download_course_data(
  zip_path = "C:/Users/yourname/Downloads/course-data-2026.1.zip"
)
```

The file `MANIFEST.tsv` must be in the same folder as the ZIP file. The function `download_course_data` uses `getPass` to ask for a masked password. A prompt asks for the password. Type it and press Enter. You will not see the letters appear. Do not write the password in this notebook, in a shared script or in your command history. Students have no separate terminal command to decrypt the archive. Both routes use the same R helper and the `archive` package. You do not need to install 7-Zip.
blocks.expected_result: R prints `Course data are ready: 105 files verified.` The data are in the folder `data/course/`. The archive and its small manifest file (a list of the files inside) must both match their configured SHA-256 values. R also checks every extracted data file.
blocks.troubleshooting: If the release address is empty, the public release is not set up yet. Use the authorised local test or ask the instructor. If the password is wrong, R shows a message that asks you to check your typing and to contact the instructor if needed. Never bypass a checksum failure. If the destination folder already exists, R refuses to continue. This protects your work. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
If the checksum differs but the password is accepted, should you use that download?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. Obtain the approved matching package before continuing.</details>
blocks.files_created: Verified data in `data/course/`. R removes the temporary download and extraction files. Data and passwords are never added to Git.
